subject.title: Interactive parity with the Codex runtime: ask-user-question · plan mode · goal mode — the roadmap

question: Should OpenClaw accept Codex-style structured questions, plan mode, and goal mode as core runtime features now, and should the paired implementation land together or be split into staged PRs?
rationale: The request adds cross-surface core runtime behavior, UI/channel delivery, protocol/API surface, and unattended goal continuation, so automation cannot safely infer the intended product and rollout shape.

options.title: Split staged PRs
options.body: Keep this hub open and require staged review of question pipeline, plan mode, and goal driver work with focused proof for each surface.

options.title: Sponsor the full branch
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the broad review cost and resolve the paired branch's current proof, source, and rollout blockers as one feature bundle.

options.title: Defer or narrow
options.body: Maintainers can keep the roadmap open but reject or postpone pieces that should wait for a smaller core/plugin API design first.

recommendation.title: Split staged PRs
recommendation.body: Keep this hub open and require staged review of question pipeline, plan mode, and goal driver work with focused proof for each surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest feature-history signal for plan/update_plan policy is steipete's experimental structured plan update work, which makes him the best available product-direction owner from the history inspected.
